common.tagline: Know what you have, what is already committed, and what the next dollar should do.

landing.headline: Your life's financial system.
landing.subheadline: Know what you have. Know what is coming. Know exactly what your next dollar should do.

footer.note: {name} organizes your finances and tells you what to do with your money. It is not a bank, it does not move your money, and it does not replace your accountant. Tax figures are estimates and are called that everywhere in the application.

demo.label: Demonstration
demo.note: Example figures, consistent with each other. None belong to a real person.

mechanism.title: Money is a level, not a number
mechanism.detail: Knowing you have $4,180 helps very little. What you need to know is how much of it already belongs to something and how much is genuinely left.
mechanism.basis: of {liquid} across accounts, with {committed} already committed

refusals.title: What this product refuses to do
refusals.detail: Almost everything below is a decision not to do something that would have been easier.

duplicates.claim: It will not import the same transaction twice
duplicates.detail: Every movement carries a fingerprint computed from the account, the date, the amount and the normalized description. Upload the same statement again and nothing happens.

transfers.claim: Paying your card is not an expense
transfers.detail: Moving money between your own accounts is not spending. Counting it would double every purchase already on the card and make a disciplined month look catastrophic.

ai.detail: It explains and it classifies; it does not compute. Every figure comes from your records, and the system rejects any answer citing a number it was not given.

tax.detail: We say estimated tax reserve, with the version of the rules that produced it. Panama's rules live in the database with their source, and nothing is shown until somebody qualified has reviewed them.

who.title: Who it is for
who.detail: The same engine, three different situations.

couples.title: Couples and families
couples.detail: Finances managed together without losing what belongs to each person. You decide what gets shared.

independents.title: Independent professionals
independents.detail: Income arrives in full and feels available. The tax reserve sets aside what was never yours, from the day it lands.

accountants.title: Accountants
accountants.detail: Explicit, scoped, revocable access. An accountant never gains access automatically.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.detail: A free plan that genuinely works, and paid plans when your situation asks for them.

close.title: Your money is complicated. Your financial system shouldn't be.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.detail: The same limits the product enforces. This table is read from the database, not from a list maintained separately.

empty.title: The plan catalogue is not loaded yet
empty.body: Prices are read from the database. With no active plans, this page invents none.

notes.title: Before you decide
notes.provisional: These figures are provisional: final pricing is not decided and this is not an offer.
notes.freeTier: The free plan is not a trial. If a subscription lapses your account returns to it, and your history stays yours.
notes.noLockIn: You can export everything inside as CSV and JSON, at any time, without asking.

blog.title: Writing
blog.detail: About money decisions, and about how this is built.

empty.title: We haven't published anything yet
empty.body: When there is something worth reading it will appear here. An empty list beats three filler articles.

empty.title: No entries yet
empty.body: What gets published here is what changed for someone using the product, not every commit.

legal.unreviewed: This text is a draft and has not been reviewed by a lawyer. It is published so you can see what it says today, not as a settled document.

missing.title: This document is not published yet
missing.body: We would rather show nothing than show a legal text nobody wrote.

signIn.title: Sign in to your system
signIn.detail: Your accounts, your rules, and your allocation plan.

signUp.title: Create your account
signUp.detail: The account first; your household and bank accounts come next.
signUp.checkYourEmail: We sent you an email to confirm your address. Open it to finish creating your account.

forgot.title: Recover your password
forgot.detail: We'll send you a link to choose a new one. It expires in an hour.
forgot.sent: If that address has an account, the link is on its way. Check your email, including spam.
forgot.rateLimited: We can't send another email right now. Wait up to an hour, or use a recovery link that already arrived in your inbox (check spam).

reset.title: Choose a new password
reset.detail: Saving it ends every other session open on your account.
reset.expiredBody: Recovery links expire after an hour and can only be used once. Request a new one.

errors.title: We couldn't continue
errors.signInFailed: That email and password don't match. Check them and try again.
errors.signUpFailed: We couldn't create the account. Please try again in a moment.
errors.passwordTooShort: The password needs at least 8 characters.
errors.linkExpired: That link has expired. Request a new one.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

onboarding.title: Let's start with your household
onboarding.detail: A household groups the finances that are managed together. It can be just you, a couple, or a family. You decide what gets shared afterwards.

fields.name: Household name
fields.nameHint: Your name, for instance, or yours and your partner's.

errors.title: We couldn't create the household
errors.createFailed: We couldn't create the household. Please try again in a moment.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Please sign in again.

overview.title: Your position

gauge.label: Safe to spend
gauge.explanation: The level falls when you commit money and rises only when money actually arrives. Everything above the surface already belongs to something.

empty.title: Give your money somewhere to live.
empty.body: Add your first account or import a statement. From there we work out what is committed and what is genuinely left.

claims.title: What claims that money
claims.detail: Commitments in the next 30 days, ordered by due date.
claims.emptyTitle: Nothing committed in the next 30 days.
claims.emptyBody: Once you record a recurring obligation it appears here and lowers what is available.

overview.planLink: See what to do with this money
overview.scopeNote: Available here deducts the obligations recorded for the next 30 days. The full calculation — minimum debt payments, estimated tax reserve and buffer — is in the plan.

plan.title: What to do with this money
plan.detail: A concrete plan for the money you have available right now, line by line, with the reason for each.
plan.basis: This plan allocates {incoming} of liquid balance. When new money arrives, the same calculation runs against that income.

empty.title: There is nothing to allocate yet.
empty.body: Add an account, record an obligation or a debt. With that we can already tell you where each dollar should go.

safeToSpend.title: What is genuinely available
safeToSpend.detail: The balance less everything already spoken for, in the order it gets covered.
safeToSpend.label: Safe to spend
safeToSpend.emptyBody: Once you record an obligation, a debt or a goal, it shows up here and lowers what stays free.

lines.title: The allocation
lines.detail: Top to bottom. Each line takes what it can from what is left.
lines.emptyBody: With no obligations, debts or goals recorded, the whole balance is free.

reason.nothingLeft: Nothing left for {label} from this money.
reason.overdueEssential: Allocate {amount} to {label} because it was due on {due} and is already late.
reason.upcomingEssential: Allocate {amount} to {label} because it is due on {due}.
reason.debtMinimum: Allocate {amount} to {label} to cover its minimum payment.
reason.taxReserve: Set aside {amount} as an estimated tax reserve. Confirm it with your accountant.
reason.emergencyFund: Allocate {amount} to {label} because the buffer comes before anything optional.
reason.highInterestDebt: Allocate {amount} to {label} because it carries the highest rate at {apr}%.
reason.expensiveDebt: Allocate {amount} to {label} because it is the most expensive debt you hold.
reason.goalByDate: Allocate {amount} to {label}, which you want ready by {due}.
reason.discretionary: {amount} is yours to spend as of {today}.
reason.partial: That is part of the {requested} it needs.

notes.paused: Contributions to {target} are paused by one of your rules.
notes.otherCurrency: A rule for {target} is written in another currency and was skipped.
notes.marked: {label} is marked {priority} by one of your rules.
notes.taxesFirst: Taxes are reserved before anything else, by one of your rules.
notes.unreachableTarget: A rule points at {target}, which is not somewhere money can go.

raised.percentOfIncoming: Your rule raises {label} to {percent}% of this money.

added.percentOfIncoming: Your rule adds {label} at {percent}% of this money.

debtOrder.title: Which debt to attack
debtOrder.detail: The order your strategy imposes. The extra goes to the first; the others keep paying their minimum.

copilot.title: Reading the plan
copilot.detail: A written summary over the same figures shown above.
copilot.disclaimer: Written by an assistant over the plan already computed. The figures come from your records, not from the assistant.

declined.budget: The assistant reached this month's usage limit. The plan above is complete without it.
declined.quality: The assistant returned something we could not check against your figures, so we did not show it. Every line of the plan explains its own reason.
declined.error: The assistant did not answer. The plan above does not depend on it.

plan.scopeNote: The plan is computed from the accounts, obligations, debts and goals you have recorded today. The tax reserve is an estimate from the rate you configured, not a calculation of tax owed.

reports.title: Statements
reports.detail: {start} to {end}. Every figure comes from your transactions; nothing is summarized or estimated.

empty.title: Nothing to report yet
empty.body: Statements are computed from your transactions. Import a bank statement and these fill themselves in.

income.title: Income and expenses
income.detail: For the period. Movements between your own accounts do not count as spending.
income.transfersExcluded: {count} movements between your own accounts were excluded. A card payment is not an expense: that spending is already in the purchases.
income.emptyBody: Import a statement and confirm its lines. Income and spending group themselves by category.

cashFlow.title: Cash flow
cashFlow.detail: What the period opened with, what came in, what left, and what it closed with.

health.title: Financial health
health.detail: Each component shows the figure it comes from. If you disagree with it, you can see exactly what with.
health.notACreditScore: This score is ours and measures only what you see above. It is not a credit score and no lender uses it.

export.title: Export
export.detail: The same rows you see here, in a file. Amounts are unformatted so a spreadsheet reads them as numbers.

reports.scopeNote: Statements are computed on demand from your transactions and never stored as a copy. A correction to an old movement moves every later balance with it.

accountant.title: Accountant portal

clients.title: Your clients
clients.detail: Every household that granted you access, with what needs attention today.

empty.title: Nobody has granted you access yet
empty.body: An accountant never gains access automatically. When a household grants it, they appear here with the scope they chose.

client.revocable: This access can be revoked at any time and without notice. When that happens, this page stops existing for you on the next request.

attention.title: What needs attention
attention.detail: What the household left outstanding, not a task list of your own.

notes.title: Notes
notes.detail: Visible to the household. This is not a private space.

empty.title: No notes
empty.body: A note about a specific transaction is more useful attached to it than loose in a list.

accountant.scopeNote: You only see what each household granted: their accounts, movements, documents and tax situation. Never who their members are, what plan they pay for, or what they asked the assistant.

errors.notFoundBody: The link may be broken, or the page may have moved.
errors.genericBody: We couldn't complete that. Please try again in a moment.

documents.title: Documents and imports
documents.detail: Upload a statement as CSV or OFX. We read every line and tell you how many are new, how many were already there, and which ones need you to look.

form.fileHint: CSV or OFX. Up to 15 MB.

errors.tooLarge: The file is over 15 MB. Export a shorter date range.
errors.unsupportedType: We read CSV and OFX for now. Export the statement in one of those formats.
errors.alreadyImported: You already imported this exact file. Nothing was created, so your transactions are not duplicated.
errors.storageUnavailable: We couldn't store the file. Please try again in a moment.
errors.noAccount: Add an account for these transactions to belong to first.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

form.summaryDetail: {found} lines read · {new} new · {duplicate} already there · {review} for you to check

history.title: Earlier imports
history.empty: You haven't imported a file yet.

documents.note: Analyzing a file does not create transactions yet. Every line gets a verdict and you confirm before anything enters your records.

noAccount.title: The account these belong to is missing
noAccount.body: A movement has to live in an account. Create yours and come back; it takes under a minute.

review.detail: From {account}, read on {when}. Tick what you want filed.
review.counts: {new} new · {duplicate} possible duplicates · {review} to check · {rejected} we could not read
review.discardConfirm: It closes without filing anything. The file is kept.
review.filed: Filed {count} movements. They count in your statements now.
review.settled: Every line in this file has already been filed.
review.scopeNote: Only what you tick is filed. A filed line keeps its origin: you can trace it back to the file it came from.

hints.new: We found nothing like it in your records.
hints.duplicate: It looks like a movement you already have.
hints.review: It resembles something you have, but not enough for us to decide for you.
hints.rejected: The line had no readable date or amount.

errors.notFound: We could not find this import.
errors.nothingSelected: Tick at least one line before filing.
errors.nothingFiled: Nothing you ticked was still waiting to be filed.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

accounts.title: Your accounts
accounts.detail: Where your money lives and what you owe. Everything else in the system is calculated from this.
accounts.scopeNote: The balance is the one you state: what your bank says today. The movements you import are the detail of how it got there, and they do not change this number on their own.

summary.liquidDetail: The sum of your current, savings, cash and wallet accounts.

empty.title: Start with one account.
empty.body: The account your pay lands in is usually the first. With its balance we can already tell you what is committed and what is left.

list.title: Accounts on record
list.detail: You can adjust a balance whenever you check it against your bank.
list.archiveConfirm: It stops counting in your position. Its movements are kept.

form.name: Account name
form.nameHint: However you recognise it. For example, "Banco General current".
form.balanceHintAsset: What you have in that account right now.
form.balanceHintDebt: What you owe, as a positive number. No minus sign.
form.maskHint: Optional, to recognise it. We never store the full number.

errors.title: We could not save the account
errors.nameRequired: Write a name you will recognise the account by.
errors.balanceInvalid: Write the balance as a number. For example, 1250.40
errors.maskInvalid: Digits only in the last four numbers.
errors.typeInvalid: Choose an account type from the list.
errors.createFailed: We could not create the account. Try again in a moment.
errors.notFound: We could not find this account.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

setup.title: Tell us how you live
setup.detail: Six short questions. With them we build your first plan today, without waiting for you to import a statement. You can skip any of them and come back later.
setup.skipAll: I would rather look around and fill this in later
setup.skipAllHint: Without these the plan has nothing to allocate yet.
setup.errorTitle: We could not save your answers

error.invalid: Check the amounts: they go as numbers, for example 1250.40
error.saveFailed: We could not save. Try again in a moment.
error.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.
error.dependentsExceedMembers: More people cannot depend on the income than live in the house.

household.title: How many people live on this money?
household.detail: A thousand dollars left over does not mean the same for one person as for a family of five. It is the number that gives everything else its meaning.
household.dependents: Of those, how many earn nothing?

income.title: What comes in, and how often?
income.detail: Salaries, fees, rent. If you work for yourself and the amount moves, mark it as approximate: the plan treats it differently.
income.name: Where it comes from
income.approximateHint: Tick it if it changes month to month. We will not use this figure as if it were fixed.

savings.title: What do you have today?
savings.detail: Your account balances and your savings. It is the starting point the plan allocates from.
savings.name: Account name

commitments.title: What do you have to pay every month?
commitments.detail: Rent, power, water, school, internet. This is what turns a balance into "what is actually left".
commitments.name: What you pay
commitments.essentialHint: What you would pay even in a bad month. The plan covers it first.

debts.title: Do you owe anything?
debts.detail: Cards, loans, a mortgage. With the rate we can tell you which to attack first and what that order saves you.
debts.name: Who you owe
debts.aprHint: It is on your statement. If you do not know it, leave it blank and add it later.
debts.minimumHint: The least you have to pay each month.

goals.title: What is all this for?
goals.detail: An emergency fund, a trip, a deposit on a house. Without a goal, the money left over has nowhere to go.
goals.name: What you want to reach
goals.dateHint: Optional. With a date, the plan works out how much to set aside each month.
goals.bufferHint: The balance you never want to go below. The plan protects it before anything optional.
